suspended_reason: The cause is loss of function of the MATERNALLY-expressed, paternally-imprinted UBE3A allele in 15q11-q13 -- typically a maternal multi-megabase DELETION, paternal uniparental disomy, or an IMPRINTING-CENTRE defect, with about 10% from a maternal UBE3A point mutation -- not a single-gene promoter switch. In neurons the paternal UBE3A is silenced by the UBE3A-antisense transcript, so only the maternal allele is expressed; the disease is DEFINED by the parent-of-origin-specific loss of that maternal allele -- a methylation/dosage state across the imprinted locus -- so there is no analyzable single-gene gamma shift to read (even the point-mutation minority is a parent-of-origin-dependent lesion that a promoter switch cannot capture). Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene DNA -> hold). This is the RECIPROCAL imprinting hold to Prader-Willi: Prader-Willi is loss of the PATERNAL genes of the SAME 15q11-q13 region, Angelman is loss of the MATERNAL UBE3A -- so the kit now holds the same chromosomal region from BOTH parental origins, demonstrating that the suspension rule keys on the LESION MECHANISM (imprinting), independent of parent-of-origin. A parent-of-origin (epigenetic) multi-gene model is future work, not a single-switch emergence.
discipline: no analyzable single-gene DNA read -> held (author's rule). Disclosed, not dropped.
